summary: Close the Dzen channel audit with a deterministic post/article/video content transformer and explicit fail-closed live-publication gate because Task 047 did not establish a qualified official public publishing contract; no provider is admitted.

impacts.evidence: Task 047 creates no remote account/provider binding; the transformer only preserves already tenant-authorized Task-020 publication/media references.
No Dzen credentials, cookies, remote requests or new persisted personal data are introduced; media remains represented by canonical UploadID references.
Task 047 adds no public TORGNEXA HTTP/OpenAPI operation.
The transformer consumes existing SocialPublishRequest/SocialMediaRef types without modifying frozen Connector/Runtime SDK-v1 roots or capability registry.
No persistence or migration is added.
The admission decision explicitly forbids private Studio/editor endpoints, browser cookies, DOM/headless automation and undocumented RPCs; live Publish fails closed.
No remote Dzen write capability is declared, so Task-017/Task-020 publication cannot accidentally route through an unqualified provider surface.
The content package preserves canonical PublicationID and UploadID references and creates no remote lineage claim.
There is no remote side effect or remote identity to reconcile in Task 047; Publish deterministically returns the unavailable gate.
No Dzen egress or webhook authority is added.
The unavailable live-publishing state is explicit and deterministic rather than surfacing opaque browser/private-endpoint failures.
There is no deployed Dzen provider state or schema to roll back; removing the transformer has no external side effect.

Fixture tests cover post/article/video transformation, article-video rejection and deterministic fail-closed live publication; provider conformance is intentionally inapplicable because no provider is admitted.
